rendering.recommended_scale: Preserve aspect ratio; prefer integer scaling and disable image smoothing. The source crops have variable width and height.

instructions: Crop ONLY by frames[id].x/y/w/h from the original RGBA PNG. This is NOT an 8x5 or fixed-size grid: 13 variable-width horizontal bands with 170 manually mapped rectangular regions. Use the full untrimmed region; do not guess sprite content from alpha or split clustered objects automatically.

tile_groups.description: Moss-covered dirt, rock, floating islands and twisted root/log walkways. Hand-place as ledges or terrain pieces; author actual solid platforms separately.
tile_groups.usage: Place in walkable terrain layer and separately author solid collider/top walking surface.

tile_groups.description: Forest-made fences, rope, lanterns, signs and other atmosphere pieces. Can layer in front of terrain.
tile_groups.usage: Place as foreground/background set dressing; no collision by default.

tile_groups.description: Organic thorns, sharp wood, toxic fungal patches and poisonous vegetation. Configure damaging trigger volumes manually.
tile_groups.usage: Place with a separate, inset damage trigger. Visual crop does not define a hitbox.

tile_groups.description: Ceiling-to-floor magic beam trap with visually inactive emitter variants and active colored energy columns.
tile_groups.usage: Place with top emitter at ceiling and receiver at floor; runtime controls beam state and damage.

tile_groups.description: Crates, carts, chests, logs, fallen trees, runestones, and other landmarks or interactable-looking props.
tile_groups.usage: Place at platform top or scene landmark. Optionally add authored object/obstacle collider.

tile_groups.description: Dangling foliage, vines, flowering canopy and suspended lanterns for overhead platforms and arches.
tile_groups.usage: Anchor the upper edge to ceiling, branch or platform underside; usually no collision.

tile_groups.description: Four painted forest panorama strips for separate slow-scrolling background planes.
tile_groups.usage: Render behind gameplay; scroll more slowly than camera, no collision.

tile_groups.description: Flower clusters, ferns, mushrooms, reeds, lily pads, and other ground- or pond-level vegetation.
tile_groups.usage: Decoration on ground/platforms or water edges; no collision by default.

interactives.description: Floor-to-ceiling magical barrier. OFF shows dim emitter/receiver; ON shows a bright energy column. Switch every 1000 ms.
notes: Use one visually compatible OFF sprite and one ON sprite; the source has five OFF alternatives and nine ON color alternatives, not one-to-one animation frame pairs.

Source sprites contain top and bottom caps within one 186-pixel-high crop. For a variable-height room, split caps and tile/repeat the beam core, or author a new beam length; stretching the entire crop may distort details.
Never infer active damage from alpha/color; switch the gameplay collider together with the explicit ON/OFF state.

notes: This tileset source is not a uniform cell-size grid like the example enemy atlas. The row and column fields are indexing hints only; all cropping must use explicit x/y/w/h.
Crop rectangles are approximate visually mapped regions, not verified pixel-perfect individual sprite boundaries. Some cells contain multiple painted objects; do not split them without art review.
The source PNG has semi-transparent/color-fringe artifacts (including neon-colored pixels in transparent-looking areas). Clean alpha and inspect each crop before production use.
Terrain is not a verified seamless autotile/Wang set. Manually align joins and author solid collider shapes separately.
Vertical beam variants are still images; the 1-second ON/OFF loop is a runtime state machine, not an authored transition animation.
Parallax strips are scenic illustrations and are not verified horizontally seamless.
The suggested colliders, render layers, and parallax speeds are implementation starting points, not engine-tested values.
There are no enemy sprites, enemy animations or projectile sprites in this manifest.
No optional alpha-based trim is supplied, because transparent edges are not clean enough to reliably measure content bounds.
